# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 63 (Bi-Vb Pc63)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc63
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 63
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining an untrained candidate
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc63
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The six rules specified at Vin IV 319 comprise the fundamental precepts against killing, stealing, sexual intercourse, lying, intoxicants, and eating at improper times; breaching any of them resets the two-year period [Bodhi 2012].
In the casuistry and "variant cases" (*vāra*) section, the Vinaya establishes that while conferring ordination upon an untrained candidate incurs a *pācittiya* for the preceptor and *dukkaṭa* offenses for the other participating nuns, the act is still categorized as a formal legal proceeding (*dhammakamma*), meaning the ordination itself remains valid and the candidate successfully becomes a bhikkhunī [Bodhi 2009].
Curated parallels exist across early Buddhist monastic traditions, including the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra in Pali, the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 123), Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 121), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Tibetan Pc 80; Chinese Pc 116), Mahāsāṅghika (Pc 98), and Mahāsāṅghika-Lokottaravāda (Pc 98) Vinayas [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports extensive internal reuse within the Pali Vinaya, sharing substantial phraseology with related ordination rules (such as Bhikkhunī Pācittiyas 64, 66, 67, 72, 73, and 75) and Khandhaka legal procedures (Kammakkhandhaka, Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka, Bhikkhunikkhandhaka), alongside cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) and *Vinayavastu* (D0001) [DharmaNexus].
